page.layout: One block of verse in the centre of the page, in italic type, with three paragraphs of lines. Below it, at the bottom right, a gathering signature "EP I-". No running head or page number.

p.i: Imperio subjecta tuo. Deus esse trinus Creditur invitis tenebris, quas mentibus almis Objicit, & propriis cadit incurabilis armis.

Non Christi vis ulla perit, dum Filius astra Deserit, & patrias sedes, aeternaque regna In terris prognatus homo. Non illa potestas Quâ mortem devicit, & omnia mortis amara Fregit, & inferno vitam produxit ab alveo, Queis mortis stat certa fides & gloria Fati. Sic age, sic Domini bellum gere servę fidelis, Sic Domino sic victor eris vincente fideli, Et Magnus majora dabit, sic gloria immatum [?] Te vehet excelsum numen, sic gloria coeli Impotet audaces animas queis gloria vilis Et meritum coeleste jacet, sonderque prophanum. Matte animo, Vir magne, Tuos, Christique triumphos Asserere, & invictas Te defensore tiaras.

Siquid ego vel Praeco quoeam, facilisque [illegible, ~3 letters] In laudes id verto tuas, nomenque per orbem Diffundi me vate velim. Mysteria Nomen Si quae habeat, Vir celse, Tuum, mysteria redde (Sepe vel externa latentia Oracula voce) Summaque diffuso fundatur Copia Cornu.

main_text.p: Note: the scan is faint and partly damaged; the stanza breaks follow the indents of the print.

page.notes: Doubtful readings marked [?] or [illegible]: "immatum" in the line beginning "Et Magnus", "facilisque" line end, and "sonderque". The Latin is a verse poem in italic, with some ink spots and damage on the scan. Printed words such as "Maste" and "Mafte" are read as "Matte" with doubt. The signature "EP I-" is the gathering mark at the foot right.
